content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.daoist-tao-teh-king-legge-gutenberg-l64-l214","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/daoist/project-gutenberg/tao-teh-king-legge.md","passage_locator":{"label":"The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics / THE TAO TEH KING, / THE TAO AND ITS CHARACTERISTICS / PART 1.; lines 64-214","start":"64","end":"214","translation":"The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Opening chapters describe the Tao as unnameable, as originator of heaven and earth, and as mother of all things; present paired contrasts as mutually arising; describe the sage's non-action, non-possessive conduct, and government; use images of vessel, bellows, valley spirit, female mystery, water, gold, and jade to teach emptiness, humility, endurance, and withdrawal after completion.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The Tao that can be trodden or named is not the enduring and unchanging Tao; without a name it is called the originator of heaven and earth, and with a name it is called the mother of all things.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Beauty and ugliness, skill and lack of skill, existence and non-existence, difficulty and ease, length and shortness, height and lowness, musical notes and tones, and before and behind are presented as arising through mutual relation or contrast.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The sage manages affairs without doing anything and conveys instruction without speech; things arise and grow without ownership being claimed, reward expected, or achievement rested in.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"In government, the sage is said to empty minds, fill bellies, weaken wills, strengthen bones, keep people without knowledge and desire, and restrain those with knowledge from presumptuous action.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The Tao is compared to the emptiness of a vessel and described as deep, unfathomable, pure, still, an honored ancestor of all things, and possibly before God.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Heaven and earth, and likewise the sages, are said not to act from a wish to be benevolent and to deal with all things or people as grass dogs are dealt with.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The space between heaven and earth is compared to a bellows that is emptied without losing power and gives forth more air when moved again.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The valley spirit is said not to die and is named the female mystery; its gate is called the root from which heaven and earth grew.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Heaven and earth endure because they do not live for themselves; the sage puts his person last and treats it as foreign, yet his person is foremost and preserved.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The highest excellence is compared to water, which benefits all things and occupies a low place that people dislike.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"A vessel should be left unfilled rather than carried full; a sharpened point cannot long preserve sharpness if continually felt; gold and jade filling a hall cannot be kept safe; after work is done and a name is becoming distinguished, withdrawal into obscurity is called the way of Heaven.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"The Tao","description":"The Tao is described as unnameable in its enduring form, originator of heaven and earth, mother of all things, mystery, vessel-like emptiness, honored ancestor of all things, pure and still, and possibly before God.","role_refs":["role:1"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"The sage / sages","description":"The sage manages affairs without action, teaches without speech, governs by reducing desire and presumptuous action, treats the people as grass dogs are treated, and puts his own person last.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4","ev:6","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Heaven and earth","description":"Heaven and earth are originated by the nameless Tao, are associated with the space compared to a bellows, do not act from a wish to be benevolent, and endure because they do not live for themselves.","role_refs":["role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:6","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Valley spirit / female mystery","description":"The valley spirit is said not to die and is named the female mystery; its gate is the root from which heaven and earth grew.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"All things / the people","description":"All things arise and grow; the people are governed by the sage and are compared to grass dogs in how sages deal with them.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4","ev:6"]}],"roles":[{"id":"role:1","label":"Ineffable origin and mother of all things","assigned_to":["fig:1"],"basis":"The passage says the enduring Tao cannot be trodden or named, is originator of heaven and earth when nameless, and mother of all things when named.","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"role:2","label":"Non-acting instructor and governor","assigned_to":["fig:2"],"basis":"The sage manages without doing, instructs without speech, governs by limiting desire and presumptuous action, and puts self last.","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4","ev:8"]},{"id":"role:3","label":"Enduring non-self-serving cosmic pair","assigned_to":["fig:3"],"basis":"Heaven and earth endure because they do not live for themselves and are also described as dealing with all things without benevolent impulse.","evidence_refs":["ev:6","ev:8"]},{"id":"role:4","label":"Undying generative mystery","assigned_to":["fig:4"],"basis":"The valley spirit is undying, named female mystery, and its gate is called the root from which heaven and earth grew.","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"role:5","label":"Recipients of growth and governance","assigned_to":["fig:5"],"basis":"All things spring up and grow without ownership being claimed, and the people are the object of the sage's government.","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4"]}],"symbols":[{"id":"sym:1","label":"Name and namelessness","literal_form":"The name that can be named; having no name; having a name","associated_figures":["fig:1"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"sym:2","label":"Mystery and gate","literal_form":"The Mystery; the gate of all that is subtle and wonderful","associated_figures":["fig:1"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"sym:3","label":"Mutually arising opposites","literal_form":"Beauty and ugliness; existence and non-existence; difficulty and ease; length and shortness; height and lowness; before and behind","associated_figures":[],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"sym:4","label":"Empty vessel","literal_form":"The emptiness of a vessel; a vessel left unfilled rather than full","associated_figures":["fig:1"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:5","ev:10"]},{"id":"sym:5","label":"Grass dogs","literal_form":"Dogs of grass","associated_figures":["fig:2","fig:3","fig:5"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"sym:6","label":"Bellows between heaven and earth","literal_form":"The space between heaven and earth compared to a bellows","associated_figures":["fig:3"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]

{"record_id":"batch.motif.daoist-tao-teh-king-legge-gutenberg-l217-l340","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/daoist/project-gutenberg/tao-teh-king-legge.md","passage_locator":{"label":"The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics / THE TAO TEH KING, / THE TAO AND ITS CHARACTERISTICS / PART 1.; lines 217-340","start":"217","end":"340","translation":"The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Chapters 10-16 present teachings on holding the souls and breath together, governing and loving the people without purposive action, the Tao producing and nourishing without possession or control, the usefulness of emptiness, the sage's rejection of sensory excess, the bodily basis of calamity, the unseen and formless character of the Tao, the qualities of ancient masters, and the return of all things to stillness and root.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The passage says the intelligent and animal souls can be held together in one embrace and kept from separating.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Undivided attention to the vital breath is described as making it pliant and allowing one to become like a tender babe.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"A ruler who loves the people and rules the state is asked whether he can proceed without purposive action.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The Tao is said to produce and nourish all things while not claiming them, boasting, or controlling them.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The wheel, vessel, and apartment are each described as useful because of an empty space or hollow interior.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The passage contrasts positive existence as serving adaptation with non-existence as serving actual usefulness.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The five hues, five notes, five flavours, chariot racing, hunting, and rare objects are described as damaging perception, mind, or conduct.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The sage seeks to satisfy the belly rather than the eyes, putting aside the latter and preferring the former.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Favour and disgrace are treated as equally fearsome because gaining favour brings fear of loss and losing it brings fear of greater calamity.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The body is identified as what makes the speaker liable to great calamity.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The Tao or One is described as unseen, unheard, ungraspable, formless, invisible, fleeting, and indeterminable.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Ancient masters of the Tao are described through comparisons to wading a winter stream, a guest in awe, melting ice, unworked wood, a valley, and muddy water.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Muddy water is said to become clear if left still, and rest is said to arise gradually when movement is allowed to continue.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"All things are said to go through activity and then return to their original state; luxuriant vegetable growth returns to its root.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"Knowing the unchanging rule leads through capacity, forbearance, community of feeling, kingliness, heaven-likeness, possession of the Tao, long endurance, and exemption from decay to the end of bodily life.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:12"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"self-cultivating person","description":"A person who holds the intelligent and animal souls together, attends to the vital breath, and cleanses mysterious sights.","role_refs":["role:1"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"ruler or administrator","description":"A person who loves the people, rules the state, and may be entrusted with the kingdom if he honours and loves it as his own person.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"the Tao","description":"The Tao produces and nourishes all things without claiming, boasting, or controlling, and is also described as unseen, unheard, ungraspable, formless, and ancient.","role_refs":["role:3","role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"the sage","description":"The sage seeks to satisfy the belly rather than the eyes and puts aside the craving of sight.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"ancient masters of the Tao","description":"Skilful masters of old who comprehended the mysteries of the Tao and were beyond ordinary knowledge.","role_refs":["role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:9","ev:10"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"all things","description":"All things are produced and nourished by the Tao and go through activity before returning to their original state.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:11"]},{"id":"fig:7","name_or_label":"one who knows the unchanging rule","description":"A person whose knowledge of the unchanging rule leads to forbearance, community of feeling, kingliness, heaven-likeness, possession of the Tao, endurance, and freedom from decay.","role_refs":["role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:12"]}],"roles":[{"id":"role:1","label":"self-cultivating practitioner","assigned_to":["fig:1"],"basis":"The person unifies souls, attends to breath, becomes like a babe, and cleanses inner sights.","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"role:2","label":"non-purposive governor","assigned_to":["fig:2"],"basis":"The ruler is associated with loving the people, ruling the state without purposive action, and administering the kingdom as his own person.","evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:7"]},{"id":"role:3","label":"producer and nourisher","assigned_to":["fig:3"],"basis":"The Tao produces and nourishes all things without possession, boasting, or control.","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"role:4","label":"formless and imperceptible principle","assigned_to":["fig:3"],"basis":"The Tao or One is described as unseen, unheard, ungraspable, formless, invisible, and beyond ordinary description.","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"role:5","label":"restrained sage","assigned_to":["fig:4"],"basis":"The sage satisfies the belly rather than the eyes and rejects sensory craving.","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"role:6","label":"ancient knower of Tao","assigned_to":["fig:5"],"basis":"The ancient masters are said to comprehend the Tao's mysteries and elude ordinary knowledge.","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"role:7","label":"beings that return to origin","assigned_to":["fig:6"],"basis":"All things go through activity and return to their original state or root.","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"role:8","label":"knower of the unchanging rule","assigned_to":["fig:7"],"basis":"Knowing the unchanging rule initiates the sequence leading to Tao, endurance, and exemption from decay.","evidence_refs":["ev:12"]}],"symbols":[{"id":"sym:1","label":"unified souls","literal_form":"the intelligent and animal souls held together in one embrace","associated_figures":["fig:1"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"sym:2","label":"vital breath and tender babe","literal_form":"undivided attention to vital breath; becoming as a tender babe","associated_figures":["fig:1"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"sym:3","label":"female bird at the gates of heaven","literal_form":"opening and shutting the gates of heaven as a female bird","associated_figures":["fig:2"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"sym:4","label":"empty utility","literal_form":"empty axle-space of a wheel, hollow vessel, and empty interior of an apartment","associated_figures":[],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"sym:5","label":"belly and eyes","literal_form":"the belly as what the sage satisfies, and the eyes as what he does not seek to satisfy","associated_figures":["fig:4"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"sym:6","label":"body as calamity-condition","literal_form":"the body that makes one liable to great calamity","associated_figures":["fig:2"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"sym:7","label":"formless invisible One","literal_form":"the One named through the Equable, Inaudible, and Subtle; the Form of the Formless and Semblance of the Invisible","associated_figures":["fig:3"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"sym:8","label":"unworked wood","literal_form":"wood that has not been fashioned into anything","associated_figures":["fig:5"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"sym:9","label":"valley","literal_form":"vacant like a valley","associated_figures":["fig:5"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"sym:10","label":"muddy water becoming clear","literal_form":"muddy water that gradually becomes clear when left still","associated_figures":["fig:5"],"taxonomy_refs":["water"],"evidence_refs":["ev:9","ev:10"]},{"id":"sym:11","label":"return to root","literal_form":"luxuriant vegetable growth returning to its root","associated_figures":["fig:6"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"sym:12","label":"heaven-likeness","literal_form":"the knower becoming king-like and then heaven-like","associated_figures":["fig:7"],"taxonomy_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev
